newsitem.title: UK: New airfreight service started by British Midland.
newsitem.headline: New airfreight service started by British Midland.

text.p: British Midland's trade-only airfreight wholesaler International Cargo Marketing (ICM) said it has launched a new ex-England express service to cities across Europe under the brand name EuroExpress'.
ICM, which uses the services of at least 40 airlines internationally, said EuroExpress' accommodates both general freight and smaller courier-sized shipments.

The new service, which was offered with effect from January 2, operates on a depot-to-airport basis under which shipments must be delivered by customers into ICM reception points located at London Heathrow, East Midlands, Birmingham and Sheffield, said an ICM statement.

"EuroExpress' is an overnight service offering the flexibility of a close-out (final delivery to depot) at the end of the working day, with shipments arriving for the start of business the next morning," the statement added.
From the airport of arrival in Continental Europe, the UK shipper or the consignee is responsible for onward transportation to the final destination.
British Midland is owned by Airlines of Britain Holdings Plc, which is 40 percent owned by Scandinavian Airlines System and the remainder by private shareholders.
